- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.  
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.00–0.10), model frequently overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion.  
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d forecast), model underestimates downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if recent 5–7 days show consistent decline.  
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize reversal; increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to ignore sentiment when price is near historical mean; if sentiment shifts from negative to neutral, adjust forecast to reflect gradual recovery.
